title: Files & formats — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: A competent, safety-first formats module — engine-backed file I/O, directories (with the Windows non-ASCII listing bug defeated), CSV, JSON, and a namespace-aware XML parser — whose one genuine standout is XML security: XXE is closed by construction, the parser refusing `<!DOCTYPE>` and `<!ENTITY>` outright, which lxml and most XML libraries get wrong by default. Everything else is a deliberate subset: XML has no XPath/XSLT/validation (the price of that refusal), HTML is a pragmatic flat index with three selectors (not an lxml DOM), archives are zip-only via Ring's minizip (no tar/gzip vs libarchive), there is no charset detection (UTF-8 only), and reads are whole-file with a 64 MB cap.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: Every lane names what actually ships, the tools it is fair to measure against, and the one thing still owed. Measured against lxml (XML/HTML) and libarchive (archives), this is a deliberately scoped, correctness-over-coverage module with one security-first standout.

lanes.lane: XML security — XXE closed by construction
lanes.engine: `xml.zig` refuses any document containing `<!DOCTYPE>` or `<!ENTITY>` — a hard failure, not sanitization — so external-entity injection is unrepresentable. Guarded: a `file:///etc/passwd` entity doc returns FALSE; ordinary and SAML-signed docs parse.
lanes.owed: The XXE footgun that has burned lxml, Java and .NET users is closed at the parser, by refusal — a security posture the category leaders default to wrong. The cost is paid honestly in the query lanes below.

lanes.engine: `file.zig`: read / write / append / copy / delete / stat (size, mtime), engine-backed, with a `pathIsUsable` screen that catches Windows-illegal characters before Zig std would crash the host DLL. Bytes and text; UTF-8 paths.
lanes.owed: 64 MB read cap (larger files return empty), no streaming/chunked reads, no mmap/seek, and `Move` is copy+delete (no engine rename). Solid for ordinary files, not for large or streamed ones (lane 12).

lanes.engine: list / walk / create / delete / count via `stz_dir_*`, and the non-ASCII listing bug fixed: Ring's native `dir()` routes through the Windows ANSI code page (Arabic + CJK names both collapse to `"??.txt"`); the engine uses the wide-W API → UTF-8, so names survive.
lanes.owed: A real correctness win (guarded: listed count == engine count over Arabic/CJK/Hebrew/emoji filenames). Deep walking is Ring-side; no parallel walk.

lanes.engine: `csv.zig`: RFC-4180 quoting (`""` escaping), configurable separator, header auto-detection, exact-round-trip type inference (`"007"` preserved). Two seam fixes: removed `eval()` on list-looking cells (arbitrary code from data), and a byte-scan number test ~156× faster than the old regex-per-cell.
lanes.owed: No multiline quoted fields — rows are split on newlines before field parsing, so a newline inside a quoted cell breaks the row; and a multi-byte separator falls back to a Ring split with no quote handling.

lanes.engine: `json.zig` (std.json) parse / serialize / pretty, and the UTF-8 trap fixed in `StzJsonToList` — Ring's own `JsonToList` loses its place on a raw multibyte byte and never reads `\uXXXX`; the engine parser does both. Plus a big-file `JsonFilterFeatures` escape hatch (GeoJSON, in-engine).
lanes.owed: The wart: the fix exists and the flat `StzJson*` helpers use it, but the `stzJson` class constructor still calls the old broken pure-Ring parser. Also no JSONPath, no streaming.

lanes.engine: A strict, namespace-aware single parser (`xml.zig`) shared with XML digital signatures (`xmldsig.zig`/SAML), with exclusive C14N canonicalization and a small local-name path grammar (`Root/Child/Leaf`, `//Leaf`, `Item[2]`). Builder escapes every value.
lanes.owed: No XPath, XSLT, or DTD/XSD validation — the deliberate price of the XXE refusal. A safe, namespace-aware subset that carries real SAML, not a full lxml.

lanes.engine: `fswatch.zig` — a cross-platform worker that snapshots (mtime, size) and diffs to `ADD` / `MOD` / `DEL` events; `stzFolderWatcher.Watch` / `Drain` / `Stop`.
lanes.owed: Polling-based — no native OS events (inotify/FSEvents/IOCP) — so it trades latency and scale for portability. Correct, but not event-driven.

lanes.engine: `html_dom.zig` — a pragmatic tokenizer + flat element index (depth recorded, not a nested tree), with `tag` / `#id` / `.class` selectors, entity encode/decode (the double-decode fix: `&lt;` survives), and the O(n²) Find fix (all class matches in one pass).
lanes.owed: Self-declared "not a spec-compliant HTML5 parser": no real DOM tree, no descendant/child combinators, no mutation, read-only. The full CSS selector + DOM builder is deferred ("slice 3").

lanes.engine: `stzZipFile` does zip read and write (create from file/dir, add, extract, list, contains) — but backed by Ring's native `ziplib` (minizip), not the Softanza engine. The engine `compressor.zig` offers only crc32 / adler32 / RLE / a bespoke codec.
lanes.owed: Zip only. No tar, no gzip/zlib as a user format, no 7z, no streaming filters — the many-format, streaming breadth libarchive is built on is absent, and even zip isn't engine-backed.
Three primitives only — no join / normalize / relative-to / glob and no pathlib-style path object. Enough to split a path, not to manipulate one.

lanes.engine: Whole-file read only, with a hard 64 MB cap; the one large-file path is the domain-specific `JsonFilterFeatures` (GeoJSON matched in-engine so a 40 MB file never crosses the bridge).
lanes.owed: No streaming or chunked reads, no iterparse, no mmap / random-access. A file larger than the cap simply doesn't load — the biggest structural limit of the plane.

lanes.engine: None for text: `codec.zig` is Base64 only, and everything is UTF-8 by design (stated across `file.zig`, `xml.zig`).
lanes.owed: No charset detection and no non-UTF-8 decoding — so a Windows-1252 CSV, a Shift-JIS document or a legacy-encoded HTML page can't be read correctly. The wild is not all UTF-8.

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The first closes a shipped-but-unwired fix and the biggest structural limit; the second broadens formats and encodings; the third is the query and path depth lxml and pathlib carry.

tiers.title: Tier A — the shipped-but-unwired fix & the size wall

items.title: Migrate the stzJson constructor to the fixed parser
items.text: The UTF-8 fix (`StzJsonToList`) already exists and the flat helpers use it — but the `stzJson` object constructor still calls the old pure-Ring parser that drops multibyte bytes and ignores `\uXXXX`. Point the ctor at the fix. Low effort, closes a silent-corruption path on the main surface.

items.title: Streaming & large-file reads
items.text: Chunked/streaming file reads past the 64 MB cap, plus iterparse-style incremental XML/JSON. Today a file larger than the cap simply returns empty — the plane's biggest structural limit.

items.title: A real archive layer
items.text: Engine-backed tar and gzip/zlib alongside zip (toward libarchive's format breadth and streaming filters) — so the archive lane is more than Ring's minizip and covers the formats data actually arrives in.

items.title: Charset detection & non-UTF-8 decoding
items.text: Detect and decode Windows-125x, Shift-JIS, ISO-8859-* (shared with the String page's legacy-charset gap), so files and pages not born in UTF-8 read correctly instead of mangling.

items.title: Multiline CSV + richer HTML
items.text: Parse fields before splitting rows (fixing newlines-in-quoted-cells), and land HTML "slice 3" — full CSS selectors, a real DOM, and mutation — lifting HTML from a flat read-only index.

items.title: XPath (or a richer query) for XML/HTML
items.text: A real query language over the safe parser — XPath is orthogonal to the XXE refusal, so it can be added without reopening the security hole. Closes the biggest lxml gap.

items.title: A pathlib-style path surface
items.text: join / normalize / relative-to / glob and a path object — beyond the three split primitives — so path manipulation is first-class, not hand-assembled.

items.title: mmap, engine rename & format sniffing
items.text: Random-access via mmap, a real engine `rename` (today Move is copy+delete), and magic-byte/MIME format detection beyond the current text heuristics.

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: Re-surveyed from `main`. The seam fixes are verified in code and guards: XXE refusal (a `file:///` entity doc returns FALSE, the SAML fixture still parses), HTML double-decode (`&lt;` survives), dir non-ASCII (Arabic/CJK filenames, listed count == engine count), and CSV/JSON non-ASCII survival end-to-end. The one live wart is real: the JSON UTF-8 fix exists but the `stzJson` class constructor isn't migrated to it. Note the `test/xml`, `test/archive` and `test/zip` directories are empty — XML/zip coverage lives under `test/file` and `test/html`. UTF-8-only and zip-only are deliberate boundaries.

Softanza's formats module chooses correctness and safety over coverage — a parser that refuses XXE by construction, a directory lister that survives non-ASCII names, profiled CSV/JSON with their traps fixed — and pays for it in breadth: no XPath, a flat HTML index, zip-only archives, UTF-8 only, and no streaming past a 64 MB read.

footer: Read from the source on 2026-09-16, from a read-only `main` worktree — Ring faces under `base/file` (`stzFile`, `stzFolder`, `stzCSV`, `stzJson`, `stzXml`, `stzHtml`, `stzZipFile`, `stzFolderWatcher`); engine `file.zig`, `csv.zig`, `json.zig`, `xml.zig` (shared with `xmldsig.zig`), `html.zig` + `html_dom.zig`, `fswatch.zig`, `compressor.zig`; zip via Ring `ziplib`; guards under `test/file`, `test/csv`, `test/json`, `test/html` (`test/xml,archive,zip` empty). Ratings reflect what the guards prove.
